top_signals.title: Who Pays for America’s Research and Development?
top_signals.summary:
When the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, the U.S. government was the unrivaled patron of American science. It funded nearly two-thirds of the nation’s research and development — much of it for defense — defining the early Cold War.
